o1.biggest_strength: It catches the two real leaks—silent delivery tracking and bra fit returns—and turns them into a practical 60-day plan with copy, portal changes and worked money numbers.
o1.biggest_mistake: It does not include a separate day-3 proactive update, which is one of the clearest fixes for the 62% of WISMO tickets arriving on days 3 to 5.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the day-3 update message and give expected savings as a range rather than mostly one planning target.

o2.biggest_strength: It directly addresses the tracking silence with a warehouse-leave email and day-3 update, gives honest ranges, and includes the fit quiz and swap-first portal changes the data points to.
o2.biggest_mistake: The portal pre-selects swap for size reasons, which risks replacing one nudge with another, and a few lines are a bit less precise or brand-safe, such as saying the parcel is with the courier at warehouse-leave and using 'spilling over'.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the size-swap nudge strong but not pre-selected, tighten the delivery-status wording, and add a refund-time guardrail.

reason: I would rather run Output 1 because it is more operationally careful, has cleaner brand-safe copy, and shows the money logic more tightly. Output 2 has the better day-3 update and ranges, but it needs a bit more cleanup on portal ethics and wording before launch.
